evidence: From t=16223975 through t=16226446, feedback positions match setpoint positions on all axes and feedback speeds are 0, indicating the robot is essentially stationary rather than executing a commanded move.
While stationary, estimated contact force_2 is persistently high at about 24.09 to 26.51 from t=16223975 to t=16226051, which is the main anomalous symptom.

During the same stationary interval, estimated contact force_1 drifts more negative from -3.55 at t=16223975 to -6.36 at t=16225853, indicating increasing external load/contact while the commanded pose is unchanged.

Estimated contact forces then collapse abruptly without corresponding commanded motion: contact force_2 drops from 26.03 at t=16226051 to 22.30 at t=16226150, 12.97 at t=16226347, -1.63 at t=16226446, and near zero by t=16226644.

Estimated contact force_0 also shows a transient reversal during the release event, from 1.97 at t=16226051 to -0.47 at t=16226150 and -6.21 at t=16226347, consistent with a mechanical load shifting or releasing.

Effort target torques remain nearly constant during the abnormal force build-up, especially effort_target_torque_1 around -13.91 and effort_target_torque_2 around -6.42, so the anomaly is better explained by external contact/load than by a commanded torque change.
The supplied signals do not identify the physical source of contact, so the exact obstruction, part, or fixture cannot be determined from telemetry alone.
corrective_actions: Stop or hold the cell in a safe state, inspect the robot/tooling/work area for a jammed part, mispositioned fixture, or unintended contact point, remove the interference, then verify that estimated contact forces return near the low post-event baseline seen after t=16226644.

Check fixture and part alignment at the held pose corresponding to feedback/setpoint positions near fpo0=-0.16, fpo1=-0.89, fpo2=1.22, fpo3=-0.33, fpo4=2.19, fpo5=-1.55, correct any misload or obstruction, then repeat the stationary hold and confirm contact_force_2 no longer sits around 24 to 26.

After clearing the cause, run a controlled restart or dry cycle while monitoring feedback position versus setpoint and estimated contact forces, then verify positions continue tracking setpoints and no sudden force collapse or spike like the t=16226051 to t=16226644 event recurs.
